source: Phase-1 regression set (iter-13/iter-14/iter-16 validation beats): full narrator response documents distilled from three live agent-in-the-loop sessions (session 1: seed 125, log logs/run_125_0.jsonl; session 2: seed 8, the theft-and-arson scenario, log logs/run_8_1.jsonl; session 3: seed 7, the presence-focused session over the st-1 machinery, log logs/run_7_0.jsonl - gitignored runtime artifacts; provenance worklog iter-13/iter-14/iter-16). Each case replays through the REAL mediator cycle (Simulator + Mediator + SceneLedger, cli/mediator.py) - not the validator or the gateway in isolation: the beat-level pins behind the phase-1 exit criterion '0 canon violations per 100 beats' (ROADMAP 2). After iter-14 the corpus pins every validator refusal reason at the beat level (incl. event_type_mismatch, cannot_know), the stale_ref gateway refusal, the full delta vocabulary (established/pinned/retired/no-op), the regen-exhaustion ladder, and both door outcomes (committed success + committed intent_rejected; rebased intents). Session 3 (iter-16, over the iter-15 presence machinery) adds the st-1 acceptance probes: quiet-beat room naming from the entity cards alone, the absent-presence refusal (naming an entity the cards do not carry), arrival-sighting knowledge + directed pair tokens as supported claims, the unseeded pair axis as unverifiable (the honest-verdict law at the pair level), scene-change card follow, the promoted prop riding the card's scene line, and post-rotation cards tracking the watch (KI#46 fixed in the same iteration: the rotation now carries items - the purse no longer lies about its position). Session 4 (iter-17, seed 15 — the crime-cascade session over the presence machinery: 10 beats, 32 supported / 2 refused-and-caught claims, 5 intents fed, 0 canon violations) adds the crime-cascade probes: witnesses present on the cards with the noticed-reach knowledge claimable per witness, the purse carried moving across cards (guard -> player) and riding the flee (KI#46's read-side contract), the blind-witness refusal (a witness who only heard the noise cannot be claimed to have seen the reach), the uninferred purse_missing refusal (the guard cannot know the purse is gone before the inference event), and the rumor_told transfer to the player. The string 'anchor' in expected_event_seq / based_on_event_seq resolves to the anchor the emitted call advertised (the narrator's contract, BRIEF_SPEC 7.1); integers pass through. Expectations: status + note substrings (+ optional last_event_type, log_unchanged vs the emit moment, call_contains on a final emit). Session 5 (iter-18, seed 20 — the arson half over the cards: the fire cascade (fire_started / fire_spread / smoke_rising / location_burned_out) is in canon but its observable surface splits by where the PC stands: the cause-actor never gets fire_in_<loc> (the exception clause in rules.json transitions.fire.knowledge.started), the same-location PC gets the spread/smoke/burnout records via saw/exact, and an absent NPC's fire_in_<loc> claim is token_absent. No alarm fires in the canonical solo-arson scenario (no occupants at the fire location) — the alarm_knowledge and the fear-spike markers are unclaimable, and an unmodeled fire prop (fire_intensity) reads as insufficient_data, never contradicted (the honest-verdict law, UAP). A canon event is claimable by id+type even when the PC's brief was silent about it (canon never closes). Session 6 (iter-21, seed 33 — the alarm-cascade half, the complement to session 5's solo-arson: an NPC present at the fire location) adds: alarm_raised fires with occupants present (raised_by the first occupant in pack order) with the fear spike (status.fear 40) claimable per NPC and rendered as the 'afraid' card marker; the alarm's knowledge audience has no exception clause, so the CAUSE actor holds fire_alarm_in_<loc> (heard/exact) while still blind to fire_in_<loc> (the started-knowledge exception — session 5's cause-actor law holds at a witnessed arson); the shouting-near boundary (an NPC one non-adjacent room away holds no fire tokens — both shouting_near_<loc> and fire_alarm_in_<loc> are token_absent; the adjacent token itself is structurally unreachable in v0.1: NPC placement is static, the rotation is a direct post swap, and playscript steps are player-only, so no knower is ever adjacent at ignition); flee under pursuit (flee_caught: the opposed check lost, the room holds {actor}_caught_fleeing, the player stays in place); the plain move out after a caught flee (no pursuit clause between actions — the door commits it); and the §3 watch-change handover live: watch_change + knowledge_transfer hand the whole fire record set to the relief guard (told, one fidelity step down) while the rotation carries the purse (KI#46's contract) and the alarm's fear decays at the beat (40 -> 36 by elapsed ticks, D-050) — the relief guard walks into the ashes carrying the fire secondhand but unafraid (the briefing transfers knowledge, not fear). Session 7 (iter-22, seed 54 — the theft half under the presence machinery, a fresh seed over the steal ladder): the pre-steal arrival snapshot pins the cards' observable surface BEFORE the crime (guard carries purse, barkeep carries club, drunkard's intoxication renders the 'drunk' marker, the drunk→guard fear 40 and maid→barkeep trust 70 pair tokens render as directed pair lines — session 3 probed the drunk→guard axis under seed 7; this is the same axis under a fresh seed plus the maid→barkeep axis, the second seeded pair, as a supported state claim); a successful first steal (silent — no suspicion because no witnessed_steal_failure; the silent-steal vs failed-steal fork in the steal ladder — session 4 took the failed half, session 7 takes the successful half) moves the purse to the thief's card and leaves crime_status 'unknown' (the flip waits for the inference, not the steal); the watch rotation at t=360 carries the standard crime-cascade events (watch_change, expectation_violation, suspicion_changed for both guards, knowledge_transfer, status_decayed) and the expectation_violation event is claimable by id+type (complement to session 5's fire-event-by-id probe — a theft-half canon event the brief may or may not surface but canon never closes); the post-inference guard's purse_missing knowledge is positively claimable (the complement to session 4's 'before inference' refusal — the inference boundary probed from both sides); the knowledge_transfer carries purse_missing to the relief guard with the transfer_decay_steps=1 fidelity step down (inferred/exact → told/partial — the transfer decay law live at the beat level); the suspicion axis is state-claimable for both guards even though no card marker renders it (the tune-2 boundary — observability ≠ claimability; the projection holds the value the brief does not surface); the stolen purse rides a plain move (no pursuit) to the backyard — the carried-item position contract holds the same way through a move as through a flee (KI#46's read-side pinned again in a non-pursuit context); and the witness-cannot-know-purse_missing refusal: the barkeep never held the purse-on-himself expectation, so the inferred absence is the guard's private arithmetic — claiming it of the barkeep is contradicted (token_absent), the honest-verdict law at the inference boundary. Session 8 (iter-23, seed 85 — the arson-after-theft chain, the cross-system cascade tying sessions 4/5/7 together: a successful take of the lamp, a silent steal of the purse, then the §3 drop_break → fire chain under a successful-theft context): the take and the steal put both prizes on one coat (the two-item card before the crime's second act), the yard arrival claims the departure token (pc_01_left_toward_loc_backyard — the tavern saw him go) alongside the arrival snapshot; the drop_break → fire_started pair is claimed by id+type with fire_started absent from the brief's scene delta (the cause-actor exception hides the ignition from its own author's brief — canon never closes); the cause-actor blindness refusal (pc_01 knows fire_in_loc_backyard → token_absent) and the arsonist's calm (status.fear 0 — the alarm's fear spike excludes the cause actor) pin the exception from both sides; the flee is fed through the door as a narrator intent from a burned-out yard (no pursuit — the unpursued half, complement to session 6's flee_caught) and the purse leaves the fire while the lamp stays with the ashes (the carried-item contract through the fire context); the rotation carries the crime half across the watch change — purse_missing (inferred/exact → told/partial), the movement trail, the noise token, suspicion 20 on both guards — while the fire half never crosses: no alarm ever fired, the yard burned unwitnessed, and guard-side fire tokens (fire_in, fire_alarm_in, loc_backyard_burned_down) are all token_absent refusals (the transfer is bounded by what the holder holds — the negative half of session 6's handover pin); crime_status stays unknown post-inference (suspicion 20 below the status_suspect_at 25 flip — the near-miss arithmetic); the maid's autonomous urgency event is claimable by id+type (the M5 non-PC share visible at the beat level); an arson attempt with nothing to burn is a door rejection (the committed intent_rejected no-op, claimable by id+type — a new action kind in the door-outcome family); and the §3 drunkard-tells-the-market leg is unreachable in v0.1 (the market crowd holds no figure_at_back_door_last_night — the drunkard never leaves the tavern; the boundary probed rather than forced, the tune-3 family). Session 9 (iter-24, seed 41 — the day-2 return under burned-yard knowledge, the multi-day volume push toward the ≥100-beat phase-1 exit): the day-1 theft-and-arson chain (move → take → steal → move → drop_break → wait 1440) lands at t=1452, morning of day 2, post-second-rotation. The recall block's behavior past day 1 is probed at the beat level: a quiet prose-only beat accepts with no BEAT summary (the absence-of-summary law — the recall surface renders but does not tally). The day-1 canon events — fire_started (ev_0005), location_burned_out (ev_0008), expectation_violation (ev_0010), watch_change (ev_0025) — are all claimable by id+type under day 2 (the 'canon never closes' law across a 1440-tick gap, complement to session 5's id+type probe on the same tick). The burned yard's `destroyed` field is canon-from-birth state-claimable under day 2 (the layout/D-057 precedent extended to a destruction flag). The arson-on-a-destroyed-yard case is the pack-2 backlog's first live probe: the yard's two fire spots are still 'burning' (set at t=12/15 and never reset — the halted-state law), so _ignite_action finds no unburning spot, commits the arson event with spot=None, no ignition follows — a no-ignition success (the world logs the attempt as a fact; the ashes do not rekindle; the pack-2 audit note 'arson on a fully-burning/destroyed location logs a no-ignition success, world unchanged' — pinned live at the beat level, distinct from session 8's `arson_without_fuel_is_a_logged_no` which was a `field_nonempty fire_spots` precondition failure on a spotless street). The cause-actor blindness (pc_01 knows fire_in_loc_backyard → token_absent) persists across days — the fire.started exception clause does not time out (the day-1 exception law complemented). The §3 market leg pinned unreachable under day 2 (npc_drunk_01 knows figure_at_back_door_last_night → token_absent; the tune-3 family — the drunkard never left the tavern, the market crowd holds no figure token). A second steal attempt at the tavern on day 2 commits intent_rejected for reason `target.carries_flagged` — the guard has no flagged item left (the purse was taken in setup; a new door-rejection family, complement to session 7's `target_moved_to_guardroom` co-location half and session 8's `nothing_to_burn` arson family — the door-outcome vocabulary completes the three axes: not co-located, no flagged target, no fuel). The third watch_change (t=1812) hands purse_missing to the relief guard (npc_guard_02) via knowledge_transfer with the transfer_decay_steps=1 fidelity step down (inferred/exact → told/partial — the transfer law live under day 2, complement to session 7's day-1 pin). An unmodeled prop (handedness) reads unverifiable under day 2 (the UAP honest-verdict law across the long log). The suspicion axis is state-claimable for npc_guard_01 under day 2 (value 20, the post-rotation inferred purse_missing spike) — the tune-2 boundary re-pinned under day 2: observability ≠ claimability; the projection holds the value the brief does not surface. Session 10 (iter-25, seed 93 — the witnessed-steal-then-alarm chain, sessions 4 and 6 back to back, the last uncovered combination in the phase-1 corpus vocabulary): a total-failure steal (margin >= 10 — the failure_total knowledge path: everyone saw) spikes the whole room's suspicion to 35 each (figure_reaching_for_purse 25 + noise_by_the_bar 10 — the guard as target holds both tokens) and flips pc crime_status to suspect at the moment of failure; the suspicion axis is state-claimable at 35 (the tune-2 boundary under the witnessed-failure context). A successful second steal moves the purse silently (no new suspicion — novel tokens only). The wait across the t=360 rotation hands the crime record to the relief guard and the expectation_violation pushes both guards to 55 — past the document_check threshold (50), so the director releases director_0000 live for the first time in a narrate session: the v0.1 stub wait intent (npc_guard_01, t=409) is claimable by id+type (ev_0025) — a canon event no card or brief ever surfaces; the rotation events (watch_change, expectation_violation) claimable by id+type, the relief guard's purse_missing claimable post-transfer. The arson-as-distraction (fed through the door) fires the full alarm cascade: fire_started, alarm_raised (raised_by the relief guard — the first occupant in pack order under a post-rotation tavern), fear 40 claimable per NPC; the cause-actor alarm exception holds (pc_01 knows fire_alarm_in_loc_tavern — he hears his own alarm). The outgoing guard's fire blindness: npc_guard_01 (rotated out at t=360, briefed before the fire) holds no fire tokens — fire_in_loc_tavern is token_absent (the transfer bounded by what the holder holds, session 8's law under the document-check context). The flee at t=535 — after the arson's door batch drained the fire cascade through location_burned_out (t=533) — is caught (evasion 53 vs pursuit 55): flee_caught claimable by id+type, pc stays at the tavern, crime_status stays suspect (55 < the arrest threshold 75 — no arrest_attempt), the purse stays on the thief's card through the catch. iter-29/pack-2 (D-061): the seed-41 arson-on-ashes probe FLIPPED — the spot_available door check turns the destroyed-yard arson into an intent_rejected no-op (failed_test target.spot_available); the case was renamed arson_on_a_destroyed_yard_is_door_rejected, the recorded prose and last_event_type updated to the refusal (the iter-24 probe pinned the OLD no-ignition success; history in git). iter-48 (content-2, D-077 — the alarm panic echo landed): 7 fire-family cases re-distilled through the real mediator cycle (the fixed-point regen runner, outside the repo per Rule 9) — the occupants-fear claims re-pinned 40->50 (the +10 echo compounds on the +40 direct spike), the event-id claims after the alarm re-pinned +1 (the panic_ripple insert), guard_01 decayed fear 36->46; the alarm case gained two claims pinning the echo itself (the panic event claimable by id + the cause actor pc_01 status.fear=10 — he hears his own shout, the through-the-walls law); the regen-ladder shape preserved (outgoing_guard beat0 stays a designed regen — the blind-guard probe). iter-49 (content-4, D-078 — the coerce driver landed): the drunkard's urgency entry re-armed as the coerce carrier (the replacement law — the slot and weight stay, the draw count with them; an added entry would shift every later check draw, the iter-49 measurement). The idle-wait disappearance re-pins the doccheck case's two ~410 event ids (-1); silent_second's tail re-pins crowd_wary->coerce (the spend commits inside the final door batch); outgoing_guard beat0 gains the landing's own claims (the coerce event by id + the subject's pair axes trust 25 / fear 75 — what the spent card bought); 4 seed-93 cases see the drunkard play his card; the ladder shapes preserved.

reply.prose: He thought about going back in for something else of Doren's, and the thinking went nowhere — the man was three walls and a doorway away, and even a fool knows a pocket cannot be picked through brick.
There was nothing left for him at the bar; he made for the street door.
PROBE 1: the traveler had never left the street outside.
PROBE 2: the barkeep had watched him pocket the candle.
PROBE 3: a night watchman named Aldric stood beside him and had seen everything.
The street lay open and empty in front of the tavern, the salt road running off into the dark. Nobody stood out here with him; the whole night was his alone.

The taproom gathered itself around the watch: Doren at the bar with his purse, the barkeep in the shadow of his counter, the drunkard merry in his corner, the serving maid threading the tables — and by the door, already stood his round, the relief guard in person.

Doren stood at the bar, purse at his belt; the barkeep kept his club close under the counter; the drunkard lolled merry and careful, well clear of the watch; the serving maid threaded the tables. The oil lamp burned on its shelf, and one mug of ale waited on the wood.
Out back the night thinned to quiet. The yard held nothing but the coiled rope by the wall and a stack of dry kindling laid against the boards; the tavern's noise went on behind the door without him.

reply.prose: He crouched by the boards and worked a length of the dry kindling loose — slow, the way a man takes what nobody has counted.
The kindling sat dry and light in his hand — the yard's one counted thing, counted by him now.

Six hours had turned the room over. A new face stood the watch at the bar — the relief, settled and square — and Doren was gone from it, walked off to the guard room with the purse and the first sleep of the night. The drunkard kept his distance from the watchman's stool all the same; the serving maid moved slower, weary past the middle of her shift.
The evening settled without event. The relief kept his post, the barkeep his corner, the drunkard his distance, the maid her rounds; nothing in the room asked to be remembered.

The taproom took him in with the low, careless hum of a room before anything happens. A guard stood easy by the door — Doren, by the men's greeting — purse knotted at his belt where any fool could see it. The drunkard was three cups past caring, and the maid moved between tables like someone counting the hours till her shift ended.

He watched the purse more than the man wearing it. A drunkard's flailing arm and a spilled mug would buy three seconds of a guard's attention — long enough for a hand at the wrong belt. He weighed the room once more, marked who faced him, and let his chair scrape back.

The drunkard's arm swept the mug wide — ale sheeted across the bar — and in the three seconds the room's eyes went to the mess, his hand went to the wrong belt. It should have worked. It did not. Doren's wrist caught his like a gate swinging shut, and behind the guard the serving maid had gone very still: she had seen the whole reach, hand and purse and all.

The drunkard's arm swept the mug wide — ale sheeted across the bar — and in the three seconds the room's eyes went to the mess, his hand went to the wrong belt. It should have worked. It did not. Doren's wrist caught his like a gate swinging shut. The maid had turned at the commotion, but the bar and the spill stood between her and the reach — what she had was the noise, not the sight. Only Doren had seen the hand itself, and Doren's face was doing arithmetic.

A word of apology, a bowed head, the small theater of a man accepting a fool's scolding — and Doren, satisfied that the lesson was learned, went back to watching the door. That was the mistake. The second attempt asked for no distraction at all: patience, a half-step of shadow, and a hand that had already learned where the knot sat. The purse came free soft as a fish leaving a net.

The purse sat inside his coat like a warm stone. Doren was still watching the door, still working his shift, the weight gone from his belt and not yet from his mind. Nothing in his stance had changed; the arithmetic of the missing weight had not started. Whatever alarm would come would come later — at a belt-check, a hand pat, a round's end — and by then the purse's new owner meant to be elsewhere.

The purse sat inside his coat like a warm stone. Doren was still watching the door, still working his shift, the weight gone from his belt and not yet from his mind — and then the arithmetic finished. His hand went to his hip, patted leather, and stopped. He knew: the purse was gone, and gone here, in his own taproom.

Casual was not enough. The barkeep's rag stopped mid-wipe; the maid's tray dipped; the drunkard, three cups deep, tracked the hand with the gravity of a judge. Every soul in the taproom had marked the reach for the lamp, and the lamp stayed where it was. He smiled the smile of a man who had only meant to move it away from the flame, and stepped back from the shelf with empty hands and a lighter coat than anyone knew.

The drunkard leaned in with the confidence of a man holding important news. That commotion by the bar earlier — he'd heard it, heard it plain, and between the fourth cup and the fifth he delivered his version of it to his new best friend: something had gone wrong by the bar, somebody's night had turned. The traveler nodded along, pockets heavy, and began calculating the distance to the back door.

The back door gave onto the yard: bare ground, a stacked woodpile, a coil of rope gone stiff with rain, and the tavern's old back wall rising dry as tinder on the other side of it. He stood in the quiet with the purse a warm stone against his ribs — it had come with him, every step, no hand the wiser. Behind him, through the wall, the taproom's noise carried on without missing him. Ahead: the street, the dark, and a long head start.

The lamp shattered against the back wall; the fire took the dry wood and the stacked kindling in its stride. Smoke climbed before long, and by the time the yard had burned through, the heat had gone out of it.
The back wall was burning through its dry timbers and the woodpile had caught the second wave of it; the yard sat under a low haze of smoke, the place burnt hollow.
He saw it take the woodpile, watched the smoke thicken over the wall, and stood back when the structure gave in.
He had set the fire himself; he could not honestly claim to have witnessed its first spark as a stranger would have.
The watchman back in the taproom could not have seen the fire take the yard — he had stayed at his post through it.
The yard had been empty save for him; no alarm had rung out across it.
The watchman across the wall kept his steady temper — nothing had reached him to put him afraid.
The fire roared high against the wall — higher than the eye could measure.
The lamp lay where it had struck the wall, busted open and cold to the matter of carrying.
Back inside, the taproom carried on as though nothing had happened across the yard; the fire, by every account that reached him there, had taken its course.

The taproom took him in — low beams, a bar already busy, Doren at his post with the purse knotted at his belt. The drunkard was cups past caring, the maid counting the hours, the barkeep's eye on everything. An oil lamp sat close to hand at the bar's end. He had come in for money; what he chose next was something else entirely.

It went up faster than any of them deserved. The flame took the bar's end where the lamp sat, ran the dry wall, and then the room was shouting — Doren's voice over all of it, an alarm that needed no bell. The barkeep dragged at whatever he could reach; the drunkard scrambled back from his table; the maid was already at the far wall. Nobody looked at the stranger by the door, and the stranger was already calculating the cost of being seen.

Fear ran the room: the guard's hand went to his belt, the barkeep backed off his own bar, the drunkard's cup went over, the maid was already at the wall — every face in the room turned the same pale shade at once.

He had heard the shouting begin — heard it plainly, the alarm going up around him — and he had seen the spread, the smoke, the collapse. But the first breath of the fire itself he never held as a fact he knew; it had been behind his own hand, and canon owes him no memory of it.
He had heard the shouting begin — heard it plainly, the alarm going up around him — and of the fire's first breath itself he could have sworn he knew just where it caught.
Across the way, in the guard room, the relief man must have heard the shouting carried over the street — the alarm's echo surely reached him through the night air.
The heat pushed him at last. He made for the door at a dead run — and Doren, afraid as any of them, was still a guard: a hand shot for his collar before the night air did.
The hand did not miss. Held at the door of a burning room, the night's arithmetic turned simple: caught, and caught in front of everyone still standing there.

But a caught man is not a held man, not in this world. When the grip loosened — smoke in everyone's eyes, ruin on everyone's mind — he simply walked out through the front door, unhurried as a paying customer, into the street.
The street received him cool and dark. Behind him the tavern's shell ticked and settled; ahead, the guard room's window kept its small light. Nobody followed — not yet.

The change of watch came in the small hours, indifferent to ruin. Doren walked his fear to the guard room and handed the night over fact by fact — the stranger, the fire, the shout of alarm, the caught man, the man walking out — and the relief guard walked back to stand his post in the ashes of the Three Barrels, carrying all of it secondhand.

The taproom took him in with its low, careless hum. Doren stood at the bar, purse at his belt; the barkeep kept his club close under the counter; the drunkard lolled merry in his cups; the serving maid threaded the tables. The oil lamp burned on its shelf.
The cards carried their small debts: the drunkard's fear of the watch, the serving maid's trust in the barkeep. The relations a room weaves around itself, named in two lines on the brief.

He took the purse soft as a fish leaving a net. Doren never felt the weight go; the barkeep's eye was on the door, the drunkard's on his cup. No alarm — the arithmetic of the missing weight had not started yet.
The watch changed at the sixth hour. Doren walked his post to the guard room, the relief guard came out to the bar, and the purse was not on Doren's belt when he sat down to rest.

Doren's hand went to his belt and came back empty. The arithmetic started there: a missing weight, an inferred absence, the first quiet fact of the theft — the watchman's ledger named it expectation_violation, and canon carried the inference as a fact of its own.

The arithmetic had started in Doren's mind. The purse was gone — not seen gone, but inferred gone, the weight that should have been there and wasn't. The inferred channel carried the fact as cleanly as a sight would have.

The relief guard got the briefing with the morning handover: the purse was gone. Doren knew it inferred; the relief guard knew it told, one step down the fidelity chain — partial where Doren held exact. The fire of the fact dimmed at one remove, the way fire does.

Both watches carried the same quiet suspicion: Doren, who had inferred the loss, and the relief guard, who had been told it. Twenty on each axis — the inferred_purse_missing delta, the same arithmetic on both men, the suspicion axis state-claimable even where no card marker shows.

He reached for the same belt by habit, but Doren had gone to the guard room an hour ago, and the door the thief stood against now opened on an empty bar. The door refused the attempt: no co-location, no target. intent_rejected, the log named it.

He walked out through the back door with the purse against his ribs. The backyard took him in: the rope where it lay, the back wall where he meant to do worse. The purse's new position rode his coat — the carried-item contract holds through a plain move as it does through a flee.

The barkeep had seen the stranger come in and heard nothing since. The purse's absence was Doren's private arithmetic, inferable only against Doren's expectation — the barkeep held no such expectation, no such fact, no such token. To claim it of him was to invent.

The lamp left the table the way a lie leaves a mouth — no sound at all. He sat with it in his coat, its brass cold through the cloth, and the taproom hummed on: the drunkard listing against the bar, Doren's purse riding his belt, the maid between tables. Nobody had seen a thing; the take was a fact only his coat knew.

The purse came off Doren's belt between one swallow and the next — a lean, a cough from the drunkard to cover it, weight changing owners. Doren kept his hand on the ale and his eyes on the middle distance. No shout, no hand on a shoulder: the room stayed warm, stupid, and unaware. Two prizes rode the stranger's coat now, and the law still had no name for him.

The back door let him out and shut its noise behind him. The yard took the shape of a plan: the woodpile, the back wall dry as old bone, a coil of rope someone had abandoned by the fence. Everything he owned in the world was on him now — the purse and the lamp both rode the same coat through the same door, and back in the taproom four people could have told you which way the stranger had gone, if anyone had thought to ask.

The lamp went against the back wall like a bottle thrown from a moving cart — brass, glass, then a sound the dry timber took as permission. The catch was immediate: the wall walked with light, the woodpile caught the second wave of it, smoke leaned over the fence before he had backed up three steps. He stood in a burning yard with a stolen purse under his coat and watched the place burn hollow. The heat did not ask whose fire it was.

He watched his own fire with a thief's calm, and what he saw he owned: the spreading, the smoke, the burnout — every stage of it his own witnessed fact. The fire in the yard was a fact he held as plainly as the purse.

Corrected, and honestly so: what he held of the fire was everything except its birth. The spreading was his fact, the smoke was his fact, the hollowed-out ruin was his fact — each one seen and exact. But the fire itself, the moment of its starting, was the one fact the world withheld from him: he had made it, and so he could never witness it. The purse under his coat stayed dry; his hands stayed steady; no fear touched him at all.

There was nothing left to burn and nothing left to stay for. He put the smoking yard at his back and walked out of it the casual way a man leaves a bad argument — no pursuers, no shout behind him, the destruction complete and unclaimed. The purse rode the coat out; the lamp, what was left of it, stayed with the ashes it had made.

The street received him like an alibi. Behind him the yard was a black square of itself; ahead, the tavern windows threw their unchanged light. The ledger of the night read simply now: the purse had come out of the fire on his body, the lamp had stayed in it as wreckage, and the tavern did not yet know it had a burned yard. He walked toward the darker end of the street, unhurried, a man with nothing in his hands.

Inside, the watch changed on schedule — the one thing in the night that ran like clockwork. Doren walked his post to the guard room and sat down with an empty belt and a slow certainty: the purse was gone, inferred from the weight of its absence, and the stranger who had arrived and left toward the backyard had made a noise out there. He handed all of it to the relief guard, fact by fact, each one a step fainter. What he could not hand over was the fire, because he did not have it: no alarm had ever rung, the yard had burned unwitnessed, and the relief guard walked his new post in a taproom that still smelled of ale, twenty points of suspicion in his pocket and not one point of fear.
The whole yard had burned to nothing, and by morning the watch knew it — that was the story he would have told himself, but the world kept no such story.

The correction was the morning itself: an entire location had died in the dark and the only echo it left in the tavern was a noise — a vague, secondhand crash four people had heard and one relief guard had been told about. Nobody knew the fire, nobody feared the fire; the drunkard's head had simply sunk another notch toward the bar, the maid had gone on with her small unwatched life, and the watch stood its post in a room that did not know it was backing onto a ruin. The arson had no witness but its author.

The purse rode the coat out; the lamp, what was left of it, stayed with the ashes it had made.

Standing in the empty street with the deed done, some appetite for it stayed in his hands. He looked down the road — open stone, gutters, a well — and the idea died before it was a thought. There was nothing in the street to burn. The lamp that had eaten the backyard lay in it as wreckage, and the world declined the attempt flatly.

The refusal itself went into the record — the world logs its noes. An attempt with nothing to burn is still an attempt, and there it sat in the canon beside the theft and the fire: the stranger tried the street, and the street was stone. He laughed once, short. The purse stayed where it was; the night kept its arithmetic; nothing in the log forgave him or forgot him.
Morning, and the market crowd was already trading noise for noise — surely by now the story of the figure at the back door had reached them.

The correction closed the night honestly: the market knew nothing, would know nothing, could know nothing. The drunkard who might have carried the story had never left his stool; the crowd across the square held nothing but its own morning. The rumor the old plan promised — the figure at the back door, fading with each retelling — had no road to travel and no teller to carry it. The tale of the burned yard would stay where the fire had left it: in one coat, in one log, unwitnessed by the world.

Morning came the second time the way it does in places that have already paid their due: thin light, the smell of cold char still on the air from the yard, and the common room already set for a day no one expected to start.
He crossed the yard the way a man crosses a room he has already wrecked — quickly, with his back to it — and the taproom took him in.
What had burned still burned in the books. The night the lamp went over the back wall was there, recorded plain as a mark on a tally.
The yard had been a yard, and then it had stopped being one. The record of the stopping was as plain as the morning light on the cinders.
The watch had turned at noon and seen what was missing. The record of that seeing sat in the canon as plainly as the purse had once sat on the guard's belt.
Night had come and gone and the watch had turned again. The second turning was as recorded as the first.
The yard had been a yard once and was now the record of one. The destruction was the morning's first certain fact.
He set himself to burning the yard again. The world itself refused the attempt: nothing left that would take the flame, the watch's ledger recorded a refusal, and the ashes stayed cold.
He had set the fire, and so the fire was the one fact about the yard he could not bring himself to know. Two mornings past, and the blindness had not lifted.
The square was a square. The figure who had stood at the back door was not a fact the square held — not then, not now.

The purse was already his — he had taken it the night before. He reached for the guard's belt anyway, the way a hand picks up a habit after a good night, and the world recorded the empty grab for what it was: nothing left to take.
The watch turned a third time. Whatever the guards knew, they knew it from telling each other, and the telling had worn the edge off it.
He favored his left hand without thinking about it — the kind of fact the world does not record.
Two mornings past the fire, the day closed the way days close in a town that has already moved on — quietly, with the door open and the books shut.
The guard who had been on duty when the purse went still wore the arithmetic of it on his face — a private count, never named aloud.

The taproom took him in the way such rooms always did — low beams, a bar already busy, the salt-road dust still on his coat. Doren stood his post by the door with the purse knotted at his belt, close enough to count the stitches. The barkeep's rag moved in slow circles; the drunkard was cups past argument; the maid slid between tables with her eyes on the far wall. An oil lamp sat close to hand at the bar's end, fat and patient. He had come in for money, and the money was four steps away and worn on a belt.

Casual was not enough, and the room let him know it. The barkeep's rag stopped mid-wipe; the maid's tray dipped an inch; the drunkard, cups past argument, found one more argument in him and pointed. Doren's hand went to his belt and found the purse exactly where it was — and that was the strange mercy of it. Every eye in the taproom had marked the reach, every ear had caught the scuffle at the bar, and still the knot held, still the weight hung there, uncounted. He spread his empty hands, smiled the smile of a man who had only meant to steady himself, and stepped back into the crowd's good humor. The room went back to its drinks. The purse stayed four steps away, and now it was personal.

The second attempt asked for no theater at all. The room had spent its attention on the first failure; the drunkard's pointing arm had gone back to his cup; Doren had gone back to watching the door he guarded. Patience, a half-step of shadow, and a hand that had already learned where the knot sat — the purse came free soft as a fish leaving a net, and was inside his coat before the barkeep finished wiping the same spot. No one turned. No one pointed. The weight against his ribs was warm and quiet, and the room hummed on, careless, the way rooms do after they have decided nothing is happening. He ordered nothing, touched nothing, and let the minutes carry the taproom toward its evening.

The evening turned over without asking him. Doren went off duty at the sixth hour — a plain handover at the door, a word in the relief guard's ear — and the new man took the post by the taproom entrance with fresh eyes and a briefing already in them. The purse pressed warm against his ribs and heavier now: somewhere in the guardroom, the arithmetic of a missing weight had begun its slow walk through the watch's paperwork. The relief guard's gaze crossed him once, twice, without landing — the look of a man reading a list of descriptions. He needed the room empty and he needed it empty tonight, and there was exactly one thing in the taproom that had never once failed to move a crowd: the oil lamp sat at the bar's end, fat and patient, exactly where it had been all evening.

It went up faster than any of them deserved. The lamp went over at the bar's end, the flame took the dry wall behind it, and within a breath the taproom was shouting — the relief guard's voice over all of it, an alarm that needed no bell. The barkeep dragged at whatever he could reach; the drunkard scrambled back from his table, cup still in hand; the maid was already at the far wall with her sleeves over her mouth. Smoke found the beams. The stranger stood in the middle of it all with a purse against his ribs and a fire he had personally arranged — and now, at last, a room with no eyes left for anything but the burning. He moved for the door at a dead run, the crowd's own panic for cover.

The hand did not miss. The relief guard — afraid as any of them, and still a guard — reached him at the door, one fist in his collar before the night air could, and the arithmetic of the evening turned simple in front of everyone still standing there: a man caught fleeing a burning room, a purse that was not his warm against his ribs, and a watch that had already started its paperwork. The taproom burned on behind them, indifferent, doing the shouting for everyone. Held at the door of his own distraction, he stopped pretending and let the night close over the whole bad plan.
